nodes.label: c. 2600–1900 BCE
nodes.title: Indus Valley civilization
nodes.name: Indus Valley civilization; seals showing seated figures (e.g. the 'Pashupati' seal) are speculatively read as proto-yoga
nodes.notes: Evidence is contested; most scholars treat any yoga link as unproven

nodes.label: c. 1500–1000 BCE
nodes.title: Ṛgveda composed
nodes.name: Composition of the Ṛgveda; √yuj appears in the sense of yoking (chariots; later the mind) alongside ecstatic seer figures (kesin; muni)
nodes.notes: Earliest vocabulary layer of the tradition; no systematic yoga yet

nodes.label: c. 1200–900 BCE
nodes.title: Atharvaveda compiled
nodes.name: Atharvaveda compiled; hymns on prāṇa (vital breath) and the ritual ascetic vrātyas
nodes.notes: Early breath and asceticism ideas that later feed prāṇāyāma and tapas

nodes.label: c. 900–600 BCE
nodes.title: Brāhmaṇas and Āraṇyakas interiorize ritual
nodes.name: Brāhmaṇas and Āraṇyakas interiorize ritual; tapas (heat; austerity) and breath control become central practices
nodes.notes: Shift from external sacrifice to internal discipline

nodes.label: c. 800–500 BCE
nodes.title: Early prose Upaniṣads: ātman-brahman and inner sacrifice
nodes.name: Early prose Upaniṣads teach ātman-brahman identity and meditation as inner sacrifice
nodes.notes: Philosophical ground for later yoga goals (liberation through knowledge)

nodes.label: c. 5th–3rd c. BCE
nodes.title: Kaṭha Upaniṣad defines yoga (chariot metaphor)
nodes.name: Kaṭha Upaniṣad gives an early definition of yoga as firm holding of the senses (chariot metaphor)
nodes.notes: First strong use of 'yoga' as a discipline of mind and senses

nodes.label: c. 4th–2nd c. BCE
nodes.title: Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad: posture and breath
nodes.name: Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad gives early instructions on posture and breath within a devotional (Rudra-Śiva) frame
nodes.notes: Early mention of body alignment and breath in meditation

nodes.label: c. 3rd c. BCE–1st c. CE
nodes.title: Maitrī Upaniṣad: six-limbed yoga
nodes.name: Maitrī Upaniṣad describes a six-limbed (ṣaḍaṅga) yoga
nodes.notes: Precursor to Patañjali's eight limbs

nodes.label: c. 6th–4th c. BCE
nodes.title: Śramaṇa movements: the Buddha and Mahāvīra
nodes.name: Śramaṇa movements: the Buddha and Mahāvīra teach meditation (dhyāna) and ascetic discipline outside Vedic orthodoxy
nodes.notes: Parallel meditation systems; mutual influence with Patañjali is debated

nodes.label: c. 200 BCE–200 CE
nodes.title: Mahābhārata and the Bhagavad Gītā
nodes.name: Mahābhārata includes the Bhagavad Gītā (karma- jñāna- and bhakti-yoga; yoga as equanimity) and Sāṃkhya-Yoga material in the Mokṣadharma
nodes.notes: Yoga becomes a broad path concept beyond meditation (Gītā 2.48 samatvaṃ yoga ucyate)

nodes.label: c. 2nd c. BCE–4th c. CE (debated)
nodes.title: Patañjali's Yoga Sūtras compiled
nodes.name: Patañjali's Yoga Sūtras compiled (~195 sūtras in four pādas); eight-limbed (aṣṭāṅga) path; Sāṃkhya metaphysics
nodes.notes: Foundational classical yoga text; teaches a steady seat for meditation rather than a posture repertoire (YS 2.46)

nodes.label: c. 4th–5th c. CE
nodes.title: Sāṃkhyakārikā: 25 tattvas and three guṇas
nodes.name: Īśvarakṛṣṇa's Sāṃkhyakārikā systematizes the 25 tattvas and the three guṇas
nodes.notes: Standard source for the puruṣa-prakṛti-guṇa framework

nodes.label: c. 5th c. CE
nodes.title: Vyāsa's Yoga Bhāṣya
nodes.name: Vyāsa's Yoga Bhāṣya becomes the standard commentary on the Yoga Sūtras
nodes.notes: Earliest extant commentary; Sūtras and Bhāṣya may have circulated as one work

nodes.label: c. 10th c. CE
nodes.title: Vācaspati Miśra's Tattvavaiśāradī
nodes.name: Vācaspati Miśra writes the Tattvavaiśāradī sub-commentary on the Yoga Bhāṣya
nodes.notes: Major interpretive layer for later Yoga-Sāṃkhya scholarship

nodes.label: c. 6th–10th c. CE
nodes.title: Tantric traditions: mantra, cakras, kuṇḍalinī
nodes.name: Tantric traditions elaborate mantra; mudrā; cakras; nāḍīs and kuṇḍalinī; Kashmir Śaivism develops
nodes.notes: Subtle-body models later absorbed into haṭha yoga

nodes.label: c. 11th–13th c. CE
nodes.title: Nāth Siddhas develop haṭha techniques
nodes.name: Nāth Siddha ascetics develop haṭha yoga techniques (bandhas; mudrās; breath retention) aimed at stabilizing bindu and breath; very few āsanas taught
nodes.notes: Origin of haṭha practice; posture is a minor limb

nodes.label: c. 15th c. CE
nodes.title: Haṭha Yoga Pradīpikā compiled
nodes.name: Svātmārāma compiles the Haṭha Yoga Pradīpikā; teaches 15 āsanas plus ṣaṭkarma; prāṇāyāma; mudrā; samādhi
nodes.notes: Most influential premodern haṭha manual

nodes.label: c. 17th–18th c. CE
nodes.title: Later haṭha compendia expand posture lists
nodes.name: Later haṭha compendia expand posture lists: Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā (32 āsanas); Śiva Saṃhitā; Haṭharatnāvalī; Jogapradīpyakā (1737; 84 āsanas)
nodes.texts: Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā; Śiva Saṃhitā; Haṭharatnāvalī; Jogapradīpyakā
nodes.notes: Posture repertoire grows but stays mostly seated and floor-based

nodes.title: Theosophy and Orientalism recast yoga
nodes.name: Theosophical Society founded (1875); Orientalist translations and Western esotericism recast yoga; haṭha yogis often dismissed as 'fakirs' by reformers
nodes.notes: Sets conditions for the modern reframing of yoga

nodes.title: Vivekananda in Chicago; Rāja Yoga
nodes.name: Swami Vivekananda at the Parliament of the World's Religions (Chicago 1893); Rāja Yoga published 1896 reframes Patañjali for a Western audience
nodes.notes: Starts modern transnational yoga; emphasizes meditation over postures

nodes.label: c. 1900–1930
nodes.title: Physical culture meets yoga; modern postural yoga forms
nodes.name: Indian physical culture merges with European gymnastics and YMCA-style fitness; modern postural yoga takes shape
nodes.notes: Scholars (Singleton; Alter) describe modern posture practice as a hybrid

nodes.title: The Yoga Institute founded (Bombay)
nodes.name: Shri Yogendra founds The Yoga Institute in Bombay (Santa Cruz); visits the US in 1919
nodes.notes: Begins institutional householder yoga in India

nodes.title: Yogananda arrives in the US; SRF founded
nodes.name: Paramahansa Yogananda arrives in the US and founds Self-Realization Fellowship; Kriya Yoga reaches the West
nodes.notes: Early large-scale Indian yoga teaching in America

nodes.title: Kaivalyadhama founded; yoga research begins
nodes.name: Swami Kuvalayananda founds Kaivalyadhama (Lonavla) and the journal Yoga Mīmāṃsā; laboratory research on yoga
nodes.notes: Start of scientific yoga research

nodes.title: Krishnamacharya at the Mysore Palace
nodes.name: Krishnamacharya teaches in the Mysore Palace yogaśālā under the Maharaja; publishes Yoga Makaranda (1934); dynamic vinyāsa sequences emerge
nodes.notes: Root of the Ashtanga; Iyengar and Viniyoga lines

nodes.title: Divine Life Society founded (Rishikesh)
nodes.name: Swami Sivananda founds the Divine Life Society in Rishikesh
nodes.notes: Source of the Sivananda lineage (Vishnudevananda; Satchidananda; Satyananda)

nodes.title: Autobiography of a Yogi published
nodes.name: Autobiography of a Yogi published
nodes.notes: Brings yoga and Kriya to a mass Western readership

nodes.title: Indra Devi in Hollywood; Jois's institute in Mysore
nodes.name: Indra Devi opens a yoga studio in Hollywood (1947); K. Pattabhi Jois founds the Ashtanga Yoga Research Institute in Mysore (1948)
nodes.notes: Yoga reaches celebrity circles; Ashtanga formally institutionalized

nodes.title: Menuhin brings Iyengar to the West
nodes.name: Yehudi Menuhin meets B.K.S. Iyengar (1952) and brings him to the West (1954)
nodes.notes: Iyengar's international teaching begins

nodes.title: First Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centre (Montréal)
nodes.name: Swami Vishnudevananda opens the first Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centre (Montréal)
nodes.notes: Spreads Sivananda Yoga across North America

nodes.label: 1961–c. 1970
nodes.title: Television yoga (Hittleman; Lilias)
nodes.name: Television yoga: Richard Hittleman's Yoga for Health (from 1961) and Lilias Folan's Lilias; Yoga and You (from c. 1970)
nodes.notes: Mass-market home yoga in the US

nodes.title: Light on Yoga published; Integral Yoga Institute NYC
nodes.name: B.K.S. Iyengar's Light on Yoga published; Swami Satchidananda opens the Integral Yoga Institute in New York
nodes.notes: Defining reference for modern āsana practice

nodes.title: Counterculture: Beatles, Woodstock, 3HO
nodes.name: Counterculture era: Beatles visit Maharishi in Rishikesh (1968); Satchidananda opens Woodstock (1969); Yogi Bhajan founds 3HO (1969)
nodes.notes: Yoga becomes a mainstream Western spiritual and wellness movement

nodes.title: Institutions consolidate (Himalayan Institute, Pune, Yoga Journal)
nodes.name: Himalayan Institute founded (1971); Iyengar institute in Pune opens (1975); Pattabhi Jois first teaches in the US (1975); Yoga Journal founded (1975)
nodes.notes: Institutions and publishing consolidate the Western scene

nodes.label: c. 1973
nodes.title: Bikram's Beverly Hills studio (hot yoga)
nodes.name: Bikram Choudhury opens a studio in Beverly Hills (heated 26-posture sequence)
nodes.notes: Origin of branded hot yoga

nodes.title: Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram founded (Chennai)
nodes.name: T.K.V. Desikachar founds Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in Chennai
nodes.notes: Individualized therapeutic Viniyoga lineage

nodes.title: Studio-yoga boom (Jivamukti, Power Yoga, Anusara)
nodes.name: Studio-yoga boom: Jivamukti (1984); Power Yoga (1995); Anusara (1997); Yoga Alliance (1999)
nodes.notes: Vinyasa and hybrid styles go mainstream in the US

nodes.title: Critical histories of modern yoga
nodes.name: Critical history of modern yoga: De Michelis's A History of Modern Yoga (2004); Alter's Yoga in Modern India (2004); Singleton's Yoga Body (2010)
nodes.texts: A History of Modern Yoga; Yoga in Modern India; Yoga Body
nodes.notes: Reframes modern postural yoga as a twentieth-century hybrid

nodes.title: International Day of Yoga proclaimed
nodes.name: United Nations proclaims 21 June International Day of Yoga (Dec 2014); first observed 2015
nodes.notes: Global institutional recognition

nodes.label: 2010s–present
nodes.title: Misconduct reckonings and ethics debates
nodes.name: Teacher-misconduct reckonings (e.g. Bikram; Anusara; Ashtanga; 3HO); decolonization and appropriation debates; trauma-informed yoga and yoga therapy grow
nodes.notes: Ethics and inclusion now part of many trainings; verify specifics before citing

edges.notes: Bishnu Charan Ghosh was Yogananda's younger brother
Desikachar was Krishnamacharya's son (also his student)
